newsitem.title: JAPAN: Malaysia's Anwar welcomes acting PM role.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Anwar welcomes acting PM role.

text.p: Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday his designation as "acting prime minister" for a period of two months has "registered well".
"Of course I'm very appreciative of this gesture by the prime minister," Anwar told Reuters Financial Television in an interview on the sidelines of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) meeting here.
"He's still the prime minister. I've been covering his duties from time to time...with his full backing and confidence.
"But certainly this registers very well in the sense that he wants the issue of political relations with me to be excellent wnd working relations have been good in the past for many years."
Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad has named Anwar acting prime minister for two months beginning next week when the premier will be in Europe mixing holidays with official business.
It is the first time in more than a decade that Mahathir -- who has had three deputies in his 16-year tenure as premier -- has named an acting prime minister in his absence.
Political analysts have viewed it as both an expression of confidence by Mahathir in his 49-year-old deputy and an opportunity for Anwar to show his mettle in the job.
In the interview, Anwar defended curbs on property and share market loans imposed by the central bank six weeks ago to prevent a speculative bubble forming in the economy.
"Some are concerned that these are panic measures. I dispute that because we have taken pre-emptive measures early enough. We don't face a problem now. There is no (property) glut now.
"The measures are necessary and critical in the management of the economy. Thus far, investors have viewed this quite positively.
"In the final analysis, what is important in economics is the fundamentals. And our fundamentals fortunately remain quite strong."
Anwar said that while an expanding money supply -- growing at an annual rate of around 20 percent this year -- was a concern, the nation's savings rate of 38 percent was a big help in this regard.
"But still there is a nationwide campaign from schools to workers to financial institutions to continue to encourage savings as a habit.

"We have always taken pre-emptive measures," Anwar said. "Where measures need to be taken early we will do it. Some may be seen to be unpopular, but for long-term sustainability, if it has to be done, it will be done."
Anwar said the government would leave exchange rate matters to the central bank and the market.
"We are fortunate that the Malaysian ringgit has been stable for many years and has been able to withstand some upheavals and minor volatility in the market," Anwar said.
Asked if the ringgit, hovering around 2.51 to the U.S. dollar, is reflecting fundamentals, he said: "I believe so."
Anwar said he raised exchange rate issues, including the appreciating yen, with his Japanese colleagues at the ADB meeting.

"Well, of course they were generally quite supportive of the view that they don't want any volatility in the yen...that would cause instability in terms of trade and investment and exchange rates. But the standard answer is that there's not much that one can do to protect (against) these uncertain developments."
Anwar said Malaysia's trade figures have shown an encouraging trend.

"We have seen in the last few months a substantial improvement in the trade balance. We have been able to export more. We have taken measures to...invite foreign investments in new niche areas like information technology..."
